data.remark:
This commit adds the T9 frontier expert for 513–1,024-bit primes while preserving the previously validated T1–T8 experts byte-for-byte. T9 uses a fixed, feedback-free 4,096-token raw_b_two_pass schedule and a shared 470,849-parameter, two-layer bit-axis BiGRU. It was warm-started from the frozen T8 checkpoint and trained for exactly 10,000 one-step AdamW updates on adjacent T9/T10 widths.

Frozen local evaluation achieved 1,000,000/1,000,000 exact one-step transitions and 9,995/10,000 exact T9 raw-input rollouts (99.95%), including 4,092/4,094 in the 1,017–1,024-bit prime tail. Repeat execution was bitwise deterministic. These are local results, not an unseen Playground score.

We thank Robby Sneiderman, Hongyue Lei, Marcos Costa Santos Carreira, and YZ for public technical discussion in the SAIR Foundation #Modular Arithmetic Challenge channel. NeuralHorner (https://github.com/Robby955/neural-horner) and the XllentAI modular_arithmetic model card (https://huggingface.co/XllentAI/modular_arithmetic/blob/f704813dc64d7c04cc9ba7dbf9a3a281c431628d/README.md) were methodological references. The T5–T9 BiGRU code, schedules, data, and weights were independently produced; no code, weights, checkpoints, replay buffers, or generated artifacts were copied.
